research_domain_title: Community Operating System, Playbooks, and Implementation Pathways
note: Architecture and developing doctrine only. The Community Operating System and playbook library are design agendas — not an operating product that generates real town plans today. No invented population trajectories, job counts, or community dashboard values. Illustrative growth questions (e.g., 500 to 5,000) are design aspirations, not forecasts.

signature_of_movement.text: Playbooks — not merely policy papers or ideology.
signature_of_movement.practical_question: Show me exactly how my town of 500 people becomes a town of 5,000 over the next 30 years.
signature_of_movement.contrast: Most political philosophies stop at what government should do. Constitutional Capitalism must answer how a real community begins and how we know if it worked.

playbook_rule.text: Every community gets a playbook. Not every community gets the same playbook. The philosophy stays the same; the implementation changes.
examples_of_difference: Delta farming community vs mountain tourism community
Timber community vs suburban bedroom community

levels.name: Case Studies
levels.question: Real communities. Real numbers. Real mistakes. Real successes.

seven_layer_architecture.title: Complete architecture
seven_layer_architecture.summary: The fuller operating architecture of the living project.

implementation_completeness_rule.text: No proposal within Constitutional Capitalism is complete until it includes an implementation pathway, measurable outcomes, estimated costs, anticipated tradeoffs, and a process for evaluation and revision.
implementation_completeness_rule.practical_test: How would a real community begin doing this tomorrow, and how would we know if it worked?

community_blueprint_hierarchy.note: Illustrative hierarchy for design — not a claim that White County or any town has an operating blueprint today.

twenty_five_year_prosperity_plan.title: 25-Year Community Prosperity Plan
twenty_five_year_prosperity_plan.summary: Every town builds its own roadmap. Milestones below are design stages, not guaranteed timelines.

make_owners.question: How do we make them owners — not just employees?

incubator_town_model.summary: Every town becomes an incubator. Resilience comes from many owners and employers, not dependence on a single large recruiter.

illustrative_contrast.rejected_default: Trying only to recruit one large employer.
illustrative_contrast.preferred_pattern: Recruit many small businesses that employ people locally.
illustrative_contrast.example_note: Illustrative arithmetic for design discussion only — e.g., ten new businesses employing eight people each — not a forecast or invented case result.

people_first_rule.text: Every implementation starts with people — not roads, grants, or buildings first.

build_your_community_surface.title: Build Your Community
build_your_community_surface.ai_role: AI organizes best practices and helps structure roadmaps — it does not make policy or replace local judgment.

community_operating_system.name: Constitutional Capitalism Community OS
community_operating_system.summary: An operating system for towns, counties, states, and nations: same principles, different implementation.
community_operating_system.revolutionary_claim: Do not make Constitutional Capitalism only a philosophy. Make it an operating system.

implementation_completeness_test.title: Implementation Completeness Test
implementation_completeness_test.purpose: Screen any proposal — education, healthcare, banking, justice, rural development, or otherwise — before it is treated as complete.

questions.text: Does it include a concrete implementation pathway a real community could begin?
Does it include a process for evaluation and revision?
Does it start from community assets and people, not only problems and grants?
Does it adapt the playbook to local conditions rather than imposing one template everywhere?
Does it strengthen ownership — homes, businesses, land, co-ops, employee ownership, community investment — not only employment?
Does it prefer resilient many-employer/owner ecosystems over single-employer dependence where feasible?
If AI is used, does it organize best practices without becoming the policymaker?

research_status.next: Phase 2.1+: draft playbook templates, asset-inventory worksheets, and pilot community evaluation protocols without inventing town outcomes; keep Community OS non-operational until sourced modules and secure product design exist
